standard.title: Create artworks that communicate ideas
standard.description: create arts works that communicate ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have no formal prior arts education assumed. They bring play-based experience with materials, mark-making and imaginative representation from early childhood contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create artworks in one or more forms that communicate an idea drawn from personal experience, imagination or observation.

nodes.label: Materials and imagination as starting points
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a material or imaginative prompt as a starting point for making — exploring what happens when they manipulate materials or act out ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Use one material or imaginative prompt to begin making something; say what the work is about.
nodes.typical_width: Use play, materials and imagination across several contexts to develop starting points for artworks; explore how different materials (paint, clay, collage, digital) produce different effects.
wider: Use repurposed objects (packing boxes, clothing) as starting points for imagining environments or characters — extend the imaginative world through making
Use a digital device to capture the making process — photograph or film steps as part of the artwork itself
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot connect materials or imagination to a communicative intent will make without purpose — subsequent nodes requiring communicative choice are blocked.

response_modes.reason: Students need experience across a range of materials and imaginative prompts to discover which spark genuine communicative intent. No single material works for everyone at this stage.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of starting points available (found objects, digital capture, music, story) is genuinely wide — students who explore multiple entry points develop richer creative agency.
success_criteria: Uses at least one material or imaginative prompt intentionally to begin making
Can say or show what their work is about

nodes.label: Making with communicative intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make a deliberate choice in their artwork — choosing what to include, how to arrange it, or what material to use — because of what they want to communicate.
nodes.minimum_width: Make one deliberate choice (what to put in, what colour, what shape) and explain why it helps communicate the idea.
nodes.typical_width: Make multiple deliberate choices across materials, arrangement and content; explain choices in terms of what the artwork is communicating.
wider: Respond to First Nations Australian visual arts or designs encountered through culturally authoritative resources — explore how specific choices (colour, symbol, pattern) communicate meaning
Create a work in response to another arts form (music, dance) — make choices about what visual elements express the feeling or story

response_modes.reason: Young students often make without reflecting on why. Simple scaffolding — 'What does your artwork show? Why did you choose that?' — builds the habit of connecting choice to intent.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cross-arts and First Nations directions offer rich contexts for exploring how different visual choices communicate different meanings — especially meaningful at Foundation level where students are discovering this connection.
success_criteria: Makes at least one deliberate choice about what to include or how to arrange the artwork
Explains the choice in terms of what the work is meant to show or communicate

nodes.label: Completing and communicating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create an artwork in one or more forms that communicates an idea from personal experience, imagination or observation.
nodes.minimum_width: Create one finished (or substantially complete) artwork and explain what idea it communicates.
nodes.typical_width: Create artworks in multiple forms (drawing, 3D, digital, collage) that communicate ideas from personal experience, imagination or observation; make choices that serve the communicative intent.
wider: Create a series of small works responding to a single idea in different forms — compare what each form can and cannot communicate
Use digital tools alongside analog materials to create a work — document the process and reflect on how each medium contributed

response_modes.reason: This node brings together material exploration and communicative intent. Students coordinate what they want to say with how to say it — the making and the meaning are unified.

success_criteria: Creates a substantially complete artwork in at least one form
Communicates an idea from personal experience, imagination or observation — can explain what the work is about
